exposure: Mode of birth (normal birth, caesarean section)
Time after birth (two months, six months)
cohort: A cohort of 96 primiparous women, including 72 with normal births and 24 with caesarean sections, observed at two and six months postpartum.
finding: The most frequent pelvic floor dysfunctions after birth were urinary incontinence and dyspareunia, which showed a spontaneous reduction by six months postpartum.
mod_finding: There was no statistical association between the mode of delivery and dyspareunia or urinary incontinence.
